performance.scope: Measured Shipping paid-wave stress fixture on this hardware. Completion/provenance passed; no smooth-frame-rate or global performance acceptance is inferred.

comparison.scope: Read-only assessment of existing reports. No new runs, GPU work, runtime or production changes. This is not a performance acceptance threshold.
comparison.causalRegressionVerdict: Not established. No matched 1.9.0 measurement is available in the examined local evidence.
findings: Current 1080p high-quality paid-wave stress has 206 peak entities, 21.55 ms mean frame time and 41 frames above 50 ms in 30 measured seconds; this is not smooth 60 FPS.

Current frame p99 216.84 ms and game-thread p99 216.50 ms, versus GPU p99 5.91 ms and render-thread p99 6.34 ms, are consistent with a game-thread-dominated tail. Aggregate percentiles do not identify individual CPU subsystem costs.

Every current >50 ms frame falls within 1.25 simulation seconds after a paid five-second wave. This associates hitches with deployment/crowd bursts without separating spawning, navigation, animation, presentation or diagnostic CPU work.

The curated 1.8.0 summary already records substantial overload hitches (208 entities, 53 >50 ms frames over 45 s, 176.17 ms p99). This establishes historical heavy-load stalls, not a matched baseline or proof that the 2.0 art has zero CPU cost.
limitations: No matching 1.9.0 timing report was found in local performance files, 1.9/1.8.1 curated QA summaries or examined QA archives.

1.8.0 context differs in quality preset (2 versus current 3), measured duration (45 versus 30 seconds), navigation, geometry and content. Raw historical report is unavailable locally; no numeric regression percentage is claimed.
Single current run includes diagnostic overhead and artificial paid-wave Aether grants; it does not establish ordinary-match frame rate or other hardware performance.

Low GPU times rule out a sustained GPU bottleneck in this measured workload, but do not exonerate model-related CPU creation/skinning cost. Profiling or a matched before/after run would be required for causal attribution.

shippingVisualReview.scope: Direct inspection of five final 1920x1080 Shipping screenshots: Cards, staged roster, expansion roster, tower-pathing frame and Iron Giant detail. This confirms the observed views only; it does not certify all animation times, runtime effects, collision behavior or universal visual quality.

observations: All 22 card entries and current model-rendered portraits are visible, including unchanged Dart Gun. Names, role labels and Aether costs remain readable without overlap.
Upgraded human faces/armor and distinct Mini Stampede versus regal Stampede portraits remain recognizable at collection size.
Staged models are visible on both halves of the Shipping arena, with clear silhouettes for the larger infantry, creatures, flyers and buildings.
Arena, bridges, border and hand panel fit inside the viewport. Hand stays behind the near Core and does not cover battlefield models.
Dense swarm formations and distant fighters are small at this overview scale; this frame is not evidence of every fine facial or weapon detail.
Bone Warden, Aether Reaper and Iron Giant appear on both sides with distinct silhouettes and materials. Reaper violet aura is visible in this paused frame.
Warden hammer, Reaper scythe and Giant plated body remain readable at battlefield scale; no missing model or conspicuous stretched mesh appears in this view.
Hand portraits for Mini Stampede, Stampede, Pulverizer and Shadow Surge are present, with readable costs and names.
Both left/right Guard towers visibly sit inward from bridge/path centerlines while Cores remain centered; arena framing and hand clearance are intact.
Tower-pathing fixture shows Boulderback, Ironclad and Twin Blades around the towers and lane. Perspective can overlap silhouettes; this still is not a movement or collision verdict.
Captured geometry separately records all four guards at absolute X = 6.76 and both cores at X = 0, with alignmentPassed true.
Iron Giant detail page displays the upgraded full model portrait, body/shield stats and complete protective-shell explanation.
Portrait, title and stat panels remain separated and readable. Lower matchup content continues below the scroll viewport as expected.
